notes: protocol.md at 7d8f270 confirms everything. Dispenser C196069 runs firmware 1.0.7.378-trunk with an angled FLEX8 head. It uses UDP 1964 or INCO TCP 7979, with no Windows DLL or SiLA. It has CSV maps, gradients, row/column/snake orders, pause/resume/abort, and the stated unverified items. It also says outright that command checks do not prove delivered volume. Caveat: the INCO TCP path was tested only against fixtures, not on hardware.

installation.md and io/canopen.py at c2a33ca confirm all of it: CANopen at 500 kbit/s over python-can (SocketCAN can0) with no vendor DLL; nodes 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 required; no rail and no gripper-less configurations. The NMT state is saved and restored on teardown, and SDO transfers are serialised under per-node asyncio locks with no channel release while a cancelled transfer runs. The barcode reader runs at 9600 baud.
